sentences.text: In the present case, some land owned by the appellants-- landowners,, falling in the revenue estate of Village Sunarian, Tehsil Thanesar, District Kurukshetra came to be acquired vide notifications RFA-368-1998, RFA- 480-1998 and RFA- 482-1998 -2- dated 20.06.1986 and 22.09.1986 issued under Sections 4 and 6 of the Act respectively.
Public purpose for acquisition of one land was to construct a link road from Sunarian to Dhanani road.

Award under Section 11 of the Act was passed by the Land Acquisition Collector on 22.01.1987 and the following assessment was made towards compensation:-
 Kind of land Rates per acre allowed.

1.Chahi, Ghair mumkin Bara Rs. 24,000/-
 Kalesar, Chakki, School and  Ghair Mumkin Panchayat Ghar.

2. Ghair Mumkin Abadi Rs. 48,000/-
 3. Ghair Mumkin Garha Khad Rs . 20,000/-
 4. Ghair Mumkin Basak Mawesain Rs. 14,000/-
 & Banjar Quadim.
3. Aggrieved thereof, the appellants-landowners filed reference petition under Section 18 of the Act seeking further enhancement.

Vide decision dated 11.11.1997, the petitions filed at the instance of appellants-landowners were disposed of while doing away with the belting system and awarding a uniform rate of Rs.24,000/- per acre for all types of lands excluding the gair mumkin for which the compensation assessed by the Land Acquisition Collector @ Rs.48,000/- was upheld.
Still aggrieved, the appellants-landowners filed the present appeal.

4. Impugning the award dated 11.11.1997 passed by the Reference Court, learned counsel for the appellant vehemently submits that the Reference Court went wrong while discarding the two sale deeds Ex.P-5 and Ex.P-6 produced on record by the appellants- landowners.

The details of the aforementioned sale deeds is extracted hereunder:-
RFA-368-1998, RFA- 480-1998 and RFA- 482-1998 -3- Ex. No. Sale deed
Village Area Cost Cost per acre Ex.P5 598/1 Dhanani 1k-6M 10,000/- Rs.60,000/- Ex.P6 486/1 Dhanani 1K 10,000/- Rs.80,000/-

Referring to the aforesaid sale deeds, learned counsel for the appellants-landowners submits that market value of the land for Village Dhanani, somewhere in the year 1982 was around Rs.60,000/- per acre and while considering that the two revenue estates i.e. Village Dhanani and Sunarian were adjacent, these sale deeds should have been considered by the Reference Court while passing the award.

He further submits that the factum of proximity of the land forming part of sale deeds Ex.P-5 and Ex.P-6 was also deposed by PW-2 namely Mam Chand in his cross-examination and the same was never rebutted by the official respondents and in such circumstances by applied suitable cut, sale deeds should have been considered while awarding compensation.

sentences.text:
On the other hand, learned State counsel submits that the sale deeds Ex.P-5 and Ex.P-6 being of different revenue estate were rightly discarded by the Reference Court especially when no Aks Shajra or site plan was ever proved on record so as to compare the location of land forming part of sale deeds Ex.P-5 and P-6 with the land under acquisition and as such, the award warrants no interference.
6.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the paper-book.
I am unable to find substance in the submissions made on behalf of the appellants-claimants.

7. There is no quarrel with the proposition of law that in the absence of sale deeds of the revenue estate relating to the land under RFA-368-1998, RFA- 480-1998 and RFA- 482-1998 -4- acquisition being available, the sale deeds pertaining to the adjoining revenue estates can be looked into for the purposes of assessment of market value.

Yet, in the absence of any Aks Shajra or site plan having been produced on record from the side of appellants-landowners for the purposes of comparing the distance as well as location of the land under acquisition pertaining to the revenue estate of Sunarian with the land forming part of sale deeds Ex.P-5 and P-6 relating to the revenue estate of village Dhanani, those could not have been treated as comparable sale instances and thus, no error can be found with the findings recorded by the Reference Court while declining the reference petition filed by the appellants-landowners.

8. The reliance placed upon by the learned counsel for the appellants-landowners to one stray line in the deposition made by PW-2 Mam Chand about the distance of land forming part of sale deed Ex.P-5 of about 4 to 5 acres to the acquired land cannot be given much weightage in the absence of any revenue document or in the site plan produced and proved on record in this regard.
9.
In such circumstances, finding no illegality or perversity with the reasoning recorded by the Reference Court, the present appeals being devoid of merits stand dismissed.
12.07.2024 (HARKESH MANUJA)
Tejwinder JUDGE
